alt: Splitting labeled items into groups of fixed sizes, one group at a time. For each group the table shows its size, how many items are left to choose from, the binomial coefficient for choosing that group, and the running product of those coefficients.

steps.caption: Group 1 takes 3 of the 10 items still unplaced: C(10, 3) = 120 ways. The running product is 120.
Group 2 takes 4 of the 7 items still unplaced: C(7, 4) = 35 ways. The running product is 4200.
Group 3 takes 3 of the 3 items still unplaced: C(3, 3) = 1 way. The running product is 4200. Every item is placed, so this product is the answer.
Group 1 takes 2 of the 6 items still unplaced: C(6, 2) = 15 ways. The running product is 15.
Group 2 takes 2 of the 4 items still unplaced: C(4, 2) = 6 ways. The running product is 90.
Group 3 takes 2 of the 2 items still unplaced: C(2, 2) = 1 way. The running product is 90. Every item is placed, so this product is the answer.
Group 1 takes 5 of the 5 items still unplaced: C(5, 5) = 1 way. The running product is 1. Every item is placed, so this product is the answer.
